sounds.name: Poly Brass
sounds.ref: In the style of early-80s synth-pop brass stabs
sounds.blurb: Bright, thick chord stabs with a brassy push at the front of every note.
sounds.how: Two sawtooth VCOs, one tuned a few cents sharp, make every note of the chord thick before the filter does anything. The 24 dB low-pass filter rests part closed and ENV-1 flicks it open and back on each chord, which gives the brassy push. ENV-2 keeps the chord at full level while the keys are down.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, a little apart
steps.why:
Brass starts with sawtooth waves, the brightest and buzziest shape, on both VCOs (the oscillators, the parts that make the raw tone).
- VCO-2 SAWTOOTH lit: VCO-2 now plays a sawtooth too. VCO-1’s sawtooth is already lit.
- MIX 5: the middle of the mixer knob, where both VCOs go into the filter at full level.
- VCO-2 TUNE +0.8 (+8 cents): VCO-2 a little sharp, so each pair of oscillators beats slowly and every note sounds wider.
- VOLUME 6: a chord of sawtooths is loud, so the master level comes down a little.
- Listen for: hold a chord and hear a slow swirl. Turn TUNE back to 0 and the chord goes still and thinner.

steps.title: Close the filter part way
steps.why:
The VCF (the filter) rests darker than the raw sawtooths, so the envelope in the next step has somewhere to open to.
- FREQ 4.5 (306 Hz): the cutoff of the low-pass filter, which keeps the lows and cuts the highs. Lower is more muffled, higher brighter.
- RES 1.5 (15 %): a slight lift at the cutoff for edge, nowhere near a whistle.
- KYBD 5 (60 %): the cutoff follows the keys part of the way, so the top notes of a chord do not go dull.
- Listen for: a warm, muted chord. LPF is lit, so this is the 24 dB low-pass mode.

steps.title: ENV-1 pushes the filter open
steps.why:
ENV-1 is an ADSR envelope (attack, decay, sustain, release): a shape that runs on every note. Sent to the filter it lifts the cutoff at the start of each chord and lets it settle, which is the brassy push.
- VCF ENV 5 (50 %): how far the envelope opens the filter. The ENV-1 button beside it is lit, so ENV-1 is the one used.
- ENV-1 A 2 (20 ms): quick but not instant, so the brightness pushes in like a breath.
- ENV-1 D 5 (324 ms), S 3.5 (35 %): the push lasts about a third of a second, then the chord settles a little brighter than the resting filter.
- ENV-1 R 4 (150 ms): the filter closes quickly when you let go.
- Listen for: a “baah” on every stab. Pull VCF ENV to 0 and the chords lose their bite.

steps.title: Shape the loudness
steps.why:
ENV-2 shapes the volume of every note. Stabs want full level while the keys are down and a clean stop when they come up.
- ENV-2 A 1.5 (11 ms): near-instant, so the chord lands on the beat.
- ENV-2 S 9 (90 %): held chords stay almost at full level.
- ENV-2 R 4 (150 ms): a short tail, so the stabs stay apart.
- Listen for: the gaps between stabs. Raise ENV-2 R to 6 and the stabs smear together.

sounds.name: PWM Strings
sounds.ref: In the style of early-80s string-machine pads
sounds.blurb: Soft string chords that shimmer while they hold and swell in slowly.
sounds.how: Both VCOs play pulse waves whose width LFO-1 sweeps back and forth: pulse-width modulation, the shimmer of string machines. A slow ENV-2 attack and a long release make each chord swell in and fade out.

steps.title: Pulse waves on both VCOs
steps.why:
Pulse waves are hollower and softer than sawtooths, a better start for strings.
- VCO-1 SAWTOOTH off, PULSE lit: VCO-1 now plays only its pulse wave.
- VCO-2 PULSE lit, MIX 5: VCO-2 plays a pulse too, and both go into the filter at full level.
- VCO-2 TUNE −1 (−10 cents): VCO-2 a little flat, so chords beat gently.
- PW 2 (40 %): just off square. One fader sets the width of both VCOs’ pulse waves.
- VOLUME 6: a chord of pulses is loud.
- Listen for: a reedy, hollow chord, still static.

steps.title: Sweep the widths with LFO-1
steps.why:
PWM (pulse-width modulation) is the shimmer. LFO-1 (a slow wave that moves other controls) sweeps both pulse widths, which sounds like many players slightly out of step.
- PWM 5 (50 %): how far the width is swept. The LFO button beside it is lit, so LFO-1 does the sweeping.
- LFO-1 RATE 4 (0.91 Hz): a little under one sweep a second. Slower drifts; faster warbles.
- Listen for: the chord now moves and shimmers. Pull PWM to 0 to hear it go still.

steps.title: Soften the top
steps.why:
The filter takes the fizz off the pulses so the chord sounds warm.
- FREQ 6.5 (1.4 kHz): the cutoff of the low-pass filter. Lower is more muffled, higher brighter and thinner.
- KYBD 6 (72 %): the cutoff follows the keys, so high voicings keep their air.
- Listen for: a smoother, darker chord with the shimmer still there.

steps.title: Swell in, fade out
steps.why:
ENV-2 (the loudness envelope, an ADSR) makes each chord swell in and fade like a string section.
- ENV-2 A 6.5 (900 ms): each chord takes nearly a second to reach full level.
- ENV-2 S 10 (100 %): held chords stay at full level.
- ENV-2 R 6.5 (1.0 s): chords fade over about a second after you let go, so one chord overlaps the next.
- Listen for: smooth changes between chords. Set ENV-2 A to 0 and the chords start like an organ.

context.pwm.depth: In this sound: how deep the shimmer is.
context.lfo.rate: In this sound: how fast the shimmer moves.
context.env2.attack: In this sound: how slowly each chord swells in.

tweaks.hear: From a slow sway to a nervous flutter.
Thinner, more nasal strings, with a deeper-sounding sweep.

sounds.name: Cross-Mod Bell
sounds.ref: In the style of 80s digital-sounding bells, made on an analogue synth
sounds.blurb: A glassy, metallic bell that rings out and fades, with a clang at the start of each note.
sounds.how: VCO-2 is tuned to an odd interval above VCO-1 and used only to shake VCO-1’s pitch at audio rate: cross modulation, the same idea as FM. That adds harmonics that do not fit a normal note, which the ear hears as a bell. ENV-1 opens the cross mod wider at the start of each note, so the attack clangs and the tail is purer.

steps.title: A pure tone to modulate
steps.why:
A triangle wave on VCO-1 is the carrier: plain and soft, so every extra harmonic you hear later comes from the cross mod.
- VCO-1 SAWTOOTH off, TRIANGLE lit: VCO-1 plays a triangle, close to a pure tone.
- MIX 0: fully left, so only VCO-1 goes into the filter. VCO-2 is still running; it just is not heard directly.
- VCO-2 TRIANGLE lit: VCO-2 needs a wave to modulate with, even though it is not in the mix.
- Listen for: a soft, flute-like note, nothing like a bell yet.

steps.title: Tune VCO-2 to an odd interval
steps.why:
For a bell, VCO-2 sits at an interval that is not a simple octave or fifth, so the new harmonics clash a little, as a real bell’s do.
- VCO-2 RANGE +22 st: nearly two octaves up (it steps in half steps). Whole octaves give a hollow, organ-like tone; odd steps give bells and gongs.
- CROSS MOD MANUAL 4 (40 %): how hard VCO-2 shakes VCO-1’s pitch all the time. This alone gives a dull metallic edge.
- Listen for: the triangle turns hard and clangy. Step VCO-2 RANGE up and down one notch at a time and hear the bell change colour.

steps.title: ENV-1 opens the cross mod
steps.why:
CROSS MOD ENV-1 lets ENV-1 add more cross mod over each note. With a quick decay the clang is strongest as the note is struck and fades as it rings, as a struck bell does.
- CROSS MOD ENV-1 5 (50 %): how much ENV-1 adds on top of the manual amount.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 6 (700 ms), S 0: full at once, then gone in under a second.
- ENV-1 R 5 (320 ms): any of it left fades quickly after you let go.
- Listen for: a bright strike that mellows. Pull CROSS MOD ENV-1 to 0 and every moment of the note sounds the same.

steps.title: A ringing loudness
steps.why:
A bell is struck once and dies away on its own, so ENV-2 (the loudness envelope) has no sustain and a long decay.
- ENV-2 A 0 (2 ms): struck at once.
- ENV-2 D 7.5 (2.3 s), S 0: the note rings for a couple of seconds whether or not you hold the key.
- ENV-2 R 6.5 (1.0 s): letting go early still leaves a short ring.
- FREQ 7.5 (3 kHz): the filter takes the harshest top off the clang.
- KEY FOLLOW 5 (60 %) on ENV-2: higher notes ring shorter, as small bells do.
- Listen for: notes that ring and overlap like chimes.

context.vco1.xmod: In this sound: the metallic edge that stays all through the note.
context.vco1.xmodEnv: In this sound: the extra clang at the strike.
context.env2.decay: In this sound: how long the bell rings.

tweaks.hear: Each step is a different bell: gong, chime, glass.
Harsher and more clangy, like struck metal.

sounds.name: Sync Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of new-wave sync leads
sounds.blurb: A tearing mono lead whose tone sweeps down at the start of every note.
sounds.how: SYNC 1→2 makes VCO-2 restart with every cycle of VCO-1, so VCO-2’s pitch changes its tone rather than its note. VCO MOD sends ENV-1 to VCO-2’s pitch alone, so each note starts with VCO-2 high and sweeps down: the tearing sound. SOLO and portamento make it a sliding mono lead.

steps.title: VCO-2 alone, synced
steps.why:
Only VCO-2 is heard, locked to VCO-1. VCO-1 still runs and sets the note, but it is not in the mix.
- SYNC 1→2 lit: VCO-2 restarts whenever VCO-1 starts a cycle.
- MIX 10: fully right, VCO-2 alone.
- VCO-2 SAWTOOTH lit, RANGE +7 st: with sync on, RANGE is a tone control. Higher snarls more.
- Listen for: a hard, nasal saw. Turn VCO-2 RANGE slowly and the tone changes while the note stays put.

steps.title: Sweep VCO-2 with ENV-1
steps.why:
VCO MOD sends ENV-1 to the pitch of the VCOs lit beside it. Only VCO-2 is lit here, so only the synced oscillator moves, and its sweep is heard as a sweep of tone.
- VCO MOD VCO-1 off, VCO-2 lit: VCO-1 keeps the note steady.
- VCO MOD ENV-1 4 (+9.6 st at the peak): how far ENV-1 throws VCO-2 up.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 6 (700 ms), S 1.5 (15 %), R 4: the sweep starts at its top the instant you play and falls over about two thirds of a second.
- Listen for: a tearing “neow” at the front of every note.

steps.title: Take the fizz off
steps.why:
Synced sawtooths are very bright. The filter tames them a little.
- FREQ 7.5 (3 kHz): the cutoff, brought down from fully open.
- RES 1.5 (15 %): a slight edge at the cutoff.
- KYBD 6 (72 %): high notes keep their brightness.
- Listen for: the same tear, smoother on top.

steps.title: One note at a time, sliding
steps.why:
A lead plays one line, and a slide between notes sounds like a bent guitar string.
- SOLO lit: one note at a time; the last key wins.
- PORTAMENTO lit, TIME 2.5 (0.10 s an octave): each note slides from the last.
- Listen for: overlapping notes slide into each other and the sweep starts again on each.

context.vco2.range: In this sound: where the sweep settles. Up for a harder tone.
context.vcomod.env: In this sound: the depth of the sweep.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: how long the sweep takes.
context.vco.sync12: In this sound: what turns VCO-2’s pitch sweep into a sweep of tone.

tweaks.hear: A snappy zap at 4, a slow vowel-like dive at 7.

tweaks.try: Turn it slowly while holding a note
tweaks.hear: The classic sync sweep by hand.

sounds.name: Solo Unison Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of 80s synth-pop bass lines
sounds.blurb: A huge, punchy bass with all six voices stacked on each note.
sounds.how: SOLO together with UNISON stacks all six voices on one key, each detuned a little by UNISON DETUNE, so every note is a wall of oscillators. A sawtooth and a square an octave down give it weight, and a short filter envelope gives each note a round thump.

steps.title: Stack all six voices
steps.why:
SOLO plays one note at a time; with UNISON lit as well (SOLO UNISON) all six voices play that one note.
- SOLO lit, UNISON lit: the two buttons together.
- UNISON DETUNE 2.5 (±13 cents): how far apart the stacked voices are tuned. More is wider and more chorused; at 0 they lock together.
- VOLUME 6: six voices on one note are loud.
- Listen for: a thick, churning saw on every note. Switch SOLO off and the stack shrinks to two voices a key.

steps.title: A sawtooth over a square, low down
steps.why:
Each voice gets a sawtooth for bite and a square for body, an octave down.
- VCO-1 RANGE 16’: an octave down.
- VCO-2 PULSE lit, RANGE 16’: VCO-2 plays a square (PW is at 0) at the same octave.
- MIX 5: both at full level.
- Listen for: a heavier, woodier low end under the saw.

steps.title: A round thump from the filter
steps.why:
The filter rests dark and ENV-1 opens it briefly at the start of each note.
- FREQ 3.5 (143 Hz), RES 3 (30 %): dark at rest, with a little honk at the cutoff.
- VCF ENV 5.5: how far ENV-1 opens it on each note.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 4 (150 ms), S 1, R 3.5: open at once, shut again in about a seventh of a second.
- Listen for: a “dum” on every note.

steps.title: Tight loudness
steps.why:
A driving bass wants notes that hit at once and stop clean.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 5, S 9 (90 %): full at once, holding nearly full.
- ENV-2 R 3 (67 ms): notes stop almost as you let go.
- Listen for: clean gaps in the eighth-note line.

context.voice.detune: In this sound: how wide the stack is. More is fatter but wobblier.
context.vcf.freq: In this sound: how much growl comes through between thumps.
context.env1.decay: In this sound: the length of the thump.

tweaks.hear: From a tight, solid bass to a wide, seasick one.
Each note gets a rubbery squelch.

sounds.name: Arpeggio Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of 80s synth-pop arpeggios
sounds.blurb: A held chord turned into a running pattern of short, plucked notes over two octaves.
sounds.how: The arpeggio plays the held chord one note at a time, upwards over two octaves. Each note is short, and ENV-1 snaps the resonant filter open on every one, which gives the pluck.

steps.title: Start the arpeggio
steps.why:
UP starts the arpeggio: hold a chord and its notes play one at a time from the bottom up.
- UP lit.
- RATE 5.5 (5.9 notes a second): a quick, even run.
- RANGE 2: press until the 2 lamp lights, so the pattern climbs two octaves before it starts again.
- Listen for: the pattern is there, but still a plain saw.

steps.title: A hollow pulse
steps.why:
A pulse wave gives a hollow, woody tone that suits plucks.
- VCO-1 SAWTOOTH off, PULSE lit, PW 2 (40 %): just off square.
- Listen for: a softer, rounder pattern.

steps.title: Pluck the filter
steps.why:
The filter rests dark and resonant, and ENV-1 snaps it open on every note.
- FREQ 3.5 (143 Hz), RES 4 (40 %): dark, with a ring at the cutoff.
- VCF ENV 5.5: how far ENV-1 opens it.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 4 (150 ms), S 0, R 4: a snap that closes again within a sixth of a second.
- ENV-2 S 6 (60 %): the notes hold a little lower than full.
- Listen for: a “pew” on every note. More RES makes it squelchier.

context.arp.rate: In this sound: the speed of the run.
context.arp.range: In this sound: how many octaves the pattern climbs.
context.vcf.res: In this sound: the ring on each pluck.

tweaks.hear: The pattern climbs four octaves before starting again.
The pattern goes up and then back down.

sounds.name: High-Pass Glass Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of airy 80s soundtrack pads
sounds.blurb: A thin, glassy pad with no low end, that drifts slowly brighter and darker.
sounds.how: The VCF is switched to high-pass, so it removes the lows and keeps the highs: the opposite of the usual filter. With some resonance at the cutoff the pad sounds glassy and airy. LFO-1 moves the cutoff very slowly so the chord keeps changing colour.

steps.title: Two sawtooths an octave apart
steps.why:
Bright sawtooths give the high-pass filter plenty of top to keep.
- VCO-2 SAWTOOTH lit, RANGE 4’ (+12 st): VCO-2 an octave above VCO-1.
- VCO-2 TUNE +1.2 (+12 cents): a little sharp, for slow beating.
- MIX 5: both at full level. VOLUME 6.
- Listen for: a bright, buzzy chord with a shimmer on top.

steps.title: Switch the filter to high-pass
steps.why:
With HPF lit and LPF off, the filter keeps everything above the cutoff and cuts what is below it.
- HPF lit, LPF off: 24 dB high-pass.
- FREQ 5.5 (654 Hz): everything below this is thinned away, so the chord loses its body.
- RES 4 (40 %): a peak right at the cutoff that makes it sound glassy.
- KYBD 10 (120 %): the cutoff rises with the keys, so every note keeps the same thinness.
- Listen for: a chord with no low end, airy and bright. Light LPF as well and it becomes band-pass.

steps.title: A very slow drift
steps.why:
LFO-1 moves the cutoff up and down very slowly, so the colour of the pad keeps changing.
- VCF LFO 3 (30 %): how far LFO-1 moves the cutoff.
- LFO-1 RATE 2.5 (0.28 Hz): one sweep about every three and a half seconds.
- Listen for: the chord getting thinner and fuller on its own.

steps.title: Slow in, slow out
steps.why:
ENV-2 makes the pad fade in and out.
- ENV-2 A 6 (600 ms), S 10, R 7 (1.5 s).
- Listen for: chords that rise and overlap.

context.vcf.freq: In this sound: in high-pass, how much body is taken away. Up is thinner.
context.vcf.res: In this sound: the glassy peak at the cutoff.
context.vcf.hpf: In this sound: makes the filter keep the highs instead of the lows.

tweaks.hear: From a full pad to a whisper of fizz.

sounds.name: Band-Pass Vowel
sounds.ref: In the style of talking-filter synth pads
sounds.blurb: A nasal, vocal pad whose “aah” slowly turns into “ooh” and back.
sounds.how: With both MODE buttons lit the filter is band-pass: it keeps only a band around the cutoff, which sounds like a vowel. High resonance makes the vowel stronger, and LFO-1 slides the band up and down so the vowel changes.

steps.title: A sawtooth and a pulse
steps.why:
Rich waves give the band-pass filter something to pick out.
- VCO-2 PULSE lit, MIX 5, VCO-2 TUNE −0.8 (−8 cents).
- PW 3 (36 %).
- Listen for: a buzzy chord.

steps.title: Band-pass with resonance
steps.why:
HPF and LPF lit together make the filter band-pass: lows and highs are cut and a band in the middle remains, like the formant of a voice.
- HPF and LPF lit.
- FREQ 5.5 (654 Hz): where the band sits. Lower is “ooh”, higher “eeh”.
- RES 6 (60 %): a strong peak, so the vowel is clear.
- Listen for: a nasal, talking chord.

steps.title: Move the vowel
steps.why:
LFO-1 slides the band up and down, so the vowel changes.
- VCF LFO 4 (40 %), LFO-1 RATE 3 (0.42 Hz).
- LFO-1 DELAY 5 (0.6 s): each new chord starts still, then the movement fades in.
- ENV-2 A 4.5 (180 ms), R 6 (700 ms): a soft start and a fading tail.
- Listen for: “aah-ooh-aah” across each held chord.

context.vcf.freq: In this sound: which vowel you hear.
context.vcf.res: In this sound: how strongly the vowel speaks.
context.lfo.delay: In this sound: how long each chord holds still before the vowel moves.

tweaks.hear: The vowel babbles twice a second.

sounds.name: Key-Follow Electric Piano
sounds.ref: In the style of early-80s synth electric pianos
sounds.blurb: A soft, bell-edged electric piano whose high notes die away sooner than the low ones.
sounds.how: Two triangles an octave apart give a mellow tone, and ENV-1 opens the filter briefly for a soft “tine” at the start. Both envelopes decay to silence, and KEY FOLLOW makes them shorter on high notes and longer on low ones, as on a real piano.

steps.title: Two triangles
steps.why:
Triangle waves are soft and round, the body of an electric piano.
- VCO-1 SAWTOOTH off, TRIANGLE lit.
- VCO-2 TRIANGLE lit, RANGE 4’ (+12 st): an octave up for the bright tine.
- MIX 3.5: VCO-2 at 70 %, under VCO-1.
- Listen for: a pure, flute-like organ tone.

steps.title: A short bright tine
steps.why:
ENV-1 opens the filter briefly at the start of each note for a soft strike.
- FREQ 6 (956 Hz), VCF ENV 3.
- ENV-1 A 0, D 6 (700 ms), S 0, R 5.
- ENV-1 KEY FOLLOW 6 (72 %): the tine is shorter on high notes.
- Listen for: a little brightness at the start of each note.

steps.title: A piano-like decay
steps.why:
A piano note fades even if you hold the key, and low notes ring longer than high ones.
- ENV-2 A 0, D 8 (3.4 s), S 0, R 5.5 (480 ms).
- ENV-2 KEY FOLLOW 7 (84 %): high notes decay much sooner than low ones. At 0 every note would ring for the same time.
- Listen for: the low chord rings while the high notes die quickly.

context.env2.kf: In this sound: how much shorter the high notes are than the low ones.
context.env2.decay: In this sound: how long a middle note rings.
context.vcf.env: In this sound: the tine at the start of each note.

tweaks.hear: All notes ring alike at 0; high notes become plinks at 10.

sounds.name: Inverted Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of 80s ambient pads
sounds.blurb: Chords that start bright, close as they hold, and open again as you let go.
sounds.how: ENV-1’s POLARITY is turned upside down, so as the envelope rises the filter closes instead of opening. The chord starts bright, darkens over a second or so, and brightens again in the release, which sounds like a tape played backwards.

steps.title: Two detuned sawtooths
steps.why:
A wide, bright chord to work with.
- VCO-2 SAWTOOTH lit, MIX 5, VCO-2 TUNE −1 (−10 cents). VOLUME 6.
- Listen for: a bright, wide chord.

steps.title: Turn ENV-1 upside down
steps.why:
POLARITY inverted makes ENV-1 work backwards: it now pushes the filter down while it rises.
- POLARITY: the lower button (inverted).
- FREQ 8 (4.4 kHz): open to start with.
- VCF ENV 4: how far the inverted envelope closes the filter.
- Listen for: every chord now darkens right away.

steps.title: Slow envelopes
steps.why:
Slow envelopes stretch the dip into a long swell.
- ENV-1 A 7 (1.3 s), D 8, S 6, R 7 (1.5 s): the filter closes over more than a second and opens again over the release.
- ENV-2 A 4 (120 ms), S 10, R 7.
- Listen for: a chord that fades darker as it holds, then blooms bright as you let go.

context.env1.polarity: In this sound: why the filter closes as the note holds.
context.env1.attack: In this sound: how long the darkening takes.
context.vcf.env: In this sound: how dark the chord gets.

tweaks.hear: An ordinary slow filter swell, dark to bright.
A longer bloom after you let go.

sounds.name: Cross-Mod Siren
sounds.ref: In the style of 80s sci-fi sound effects
sounds.blurb: A warbling, alarm-like tone with a metallic rasp that grows over each note.
sounds.how: VCO-2 is turned down into LOW, where it stops following the keys and runs at a few cycles a second. Used as the cross-mod source it becomes a second LFO that wobbles VCO-1’s pitch. ENV-1 then adds more and more cross mod as the note goes on.

steps.title: VCO-2 into LOW
steps.why:
At LOW, VCO-2 is a slow modulator that ignores the keyboard.
- VCO-2 RANGE LOW 7.4 Hz: five steps from the left end.
- VCO-2 TRIANGLE lit, MIX 0: VCO-2 is not heard directly, only used for cross mod.
- Listen for: no change yet, just VCO-1’s saw.

steps.title: Cross mod as a siren
steps.why:
CROSS MOD lets VCO-2 move VCO-1’s pitch. At a few cycles a second that is a wide warble.
- CROSS MOD MANUAL 6 (60 %): about an octave of swing.
- Listen for: a two-tone siren.

steps.title: Let ENV-1 widen it
steps.why:
CROSS MOD ENV-1 adds more as ENV-1 rises, so the siren starts gentle and grows wild.
- CROSS MOD ENV-1 8 (80 %).
- ENV-1 A 7.5 (2 s), D 8, S 10, R 5.
- ENV-2 R 6 (700 ms).
- FREQ 7 (2 kHz), RES 3 (30 %).
- Listen for: the warble widening over two seconds.

context.vco2.range: In this sound: the speed of the siren. Step it right for faster, until it reaches audio and turns to rasp.
context.vco1.xmod: In this sound: how wide the siren swings.

tweaks.hear: From a slow wail to a fast, growling buzz.
A steady siren that does not grow.

sounds.name: Noise Snare
sounds.ref: In the style of early drum-machine snares
sounds.blurb: A short snare hit: a pitched thump with a burst of noise on top.
sounds.how: VCO-1’s triangle is the drum’s body, given a quick pitch drop by ENV-1, and VCO-2’s NOISE is the snare rattle. ENV-2 has no sustain, so every hit is short however long the key is held.

steps.title: A body and a rattle
steps.why:
A drum is a short tone plus noise.
